diagnosis.conclusion: RTL matches the bit-level golden on every layer for all samples, but top1 does NOT track the sample class -- it collapses to a single class (1 (violin)=4, 2 (clarinet)=1, 4 (saxophone)=3). The quantized model has no class-discriminative power in the golden mel feature domain, so the constant-top1 symptom is rooted model/feature-side, not in RTL numeric correctness nor in board data transport. The board collapse point (top1=6, guitar_acoustic) differs from the RTL/golden collapse point (top1=0, piano), which indicates the board input domain additionally shifts the collapse point, but a board-side fix alone cannot restore correct classification while the model side stays non-discriminative.
suggested_next_steps: run the same 8 wavs through the InstRec floating-point model with its training-time librosa feature extractor to check whether the collapse is a quantized-model defect or a golden-mel-domain vs training-domain mismatch (dB normalization / top_db / downmix semantics)
compare golden_pipeline.run_mel_pipeline output against InstRec extract_mel on one IRMAS sample element-wise
board side stays suspect only for the collapse-point shift (6 vs 0) and for input-domain correctness, not for NPU numeric transport (RTL == golden everywhere)
